critique: The orange-on-black palette and strong upward displacement from t1 to t4 communicate rising embers, with a denser central source than earlier attempts. However, the t4 field expands into a very broad, almost explosive spray that reaches/crops at the top edge rather than retaining a tapered vertical plume. The particles remain uniformly round glowing dots; the 30 feather makes their edges too bokeh-like and prevents a sharper, hotter ember appearance. The intended Smoke-and-Fire look needs a more concentrated lower core and a more coherent upward column with only moderate lateral drift.

suggestions.why: Reduce emitter width so the source remains concentrated and the rising field reads as a tapered plume instead of a wide burst.
Narrow the directional spread to preserve clear upward flow while retaining enough variation for natural ember drift.
Lower feathering to make embers less uniformly soft/bokeh-like and give the fiery particles a crisper, hotter visual character.
Reduce velocity so particles do not disperse and crop at the top so quickly, maintaining a denser visible plume through the frame.
